2Estrutura e organização

Trabalho de congresso em 6 páginas, organizado em: resumo e abstract bilíngues; Introdução; Material e Métodos; Resultados e Discussão (subdividida em Fissuras, Fotodegradação, Conexões, Fungos, Colonização de insetos); Conclusão; Referências (10 itens). Contém 1 figura (Quiosque do Coco, foto de Pedro Devani, 2014) e 1 gráfico de patologias (fonte: próprio autor) — p. 2 e p. 3.

A obra estudada: "Quiosque do Coco", equipamento do Parque do Tucumã, Bairro Distrito Industrial, Rio Branco-AC, executado em parceria entre a Casa Civil (idealizadora), com assessoria técnica da FUNTAC e da Embrapa Acre, combinando alvenaria de tijolos furados, bases em concreto armado, telha de madeira e estrutura de cobertura com bambu nativo (p. 2). Projeto arquitetônico baseado em construções colombianas e asiáticas (Sgorla & Neves, 2017, citado na p. 2).

3Problema e perguntas de pesquisa

O uso do bambu como elemento construtivo exige a disseminação de técnicas que garantam durabilidade: do manejo à construção, agentes do meio ambiente podem comprometer a resistência das peças (p. 1). O pouco conhecimento sobre qualidades e técnicas de uso e processamento tende a oferecer um produto de baixa durabilidade e vulnerável a pragas, como brocas (Júnior, 2019, citado na p. 2). Essa situação pode ser mitigada pela identificação de erros e acertos nas etapas de processamento por meio do reconhecimento das patologias construtivas (Júnior, 2019, citado na p. 2).

Objetivo: identificar sintomas patológicos na estrutura de bambu do Quiosque do Coco, Rio Branco-AC, analisando aspectos construtivos, uso e manutenção das instalações e registrando os sintomas existentes (p. 2).

4Referencial teórico

O referencial mobiliza: INBAR (2025) — oferta mundial de bambu concentrada na China (cerca de 7,5 milhões de hectares, cerca de 75 bilhões de dólares gerados em 2023 e 15 milhões de empregos); Afonso & Silva (2017) — 258 espécies de bambu no Brasil em 35 gêneros, cerca de 20% do total mundial; o gênero Guadua como um dos mais importantes para uso em construções; Judziewicz et al. (citado por Manhães, 2008), Silveira (2001) e INBAR (2025) — maior reserva de bambu nativo do planeta na Amazônia, com maior concentração no Acre, chegando a 180.000 km²; Júnior (2019) — resistência física e mecânica do bambu que, dependendo do uso, pode superar madeira e aço, mas com vulnerabilidade por desconhecimento técnico; Hidalgo (2003) — comprometimento da peça ligado ao conjunto de fibras longitudinais; Mesquita Júnior (2019) — estudo de caso de patologias em estrutura de bambu (OCA, SINPRO); Sgorla & Neves (2017) — projeto do Quiosque do Tucumã; ABNT NBR 5674:2024 — manutenção de edificações (todas citadas entre p. 1 e p. 6).

5Metodologia

Estudo de caso com pesquisa qualiquantitativa e levantamento quantitativo das manifestações patológicas (p. 3). Procedimentos: obtenção do projeto e identificação das peças afetadas; inspeção visual e táctil dos colmos, com registro fotográfico e anotação do tipo de manifestação; método de avaliação não destrutiva (obra em uso), sem retirada de amostras para ensaios laboratoriais; por inexistência de norma específica para bambu, empregaram-se procedimentos orientados a madeira, com base na ABNT NBR 5674:2024 (p. 3).

Características da obra (p. 2-3): pilares de bambu chumbados em pilaretes de concreto armado (50 cm de diâmetro e 1 m de altura); estrutura da cobertura em bambu com telhas de madeira sobre ripas também de madeira; bambus coletados nos municípios de Porto Acre e Assis Brasil, ambos da espécie Guadua sp. (conforme Graciano & Filgueiras, 2015, e relatório não publicado); tempo de construção de cerca de 11 anos e ausência de manutenção.

Tratamento das peças (p. 3): varas de Assis Brasil tratadas em Rio Branco com furos no diafragma (nó), último diafragma intacto, solução química à base de InKabor a 5% em relação ao volume de água, despejada por dentro do bambu na posição vertical, repetida diariamente por 7 dias; varas de Porto Acre tratadas por imersão em tanque metálico por 7 dias no próprio local, com a mesma solução (InKabor a 5%); após o tratamento, secagem natural à sombra por pelo menos uma semana. Experiências de secagem em estufa descartaram cerca de 8% das peças por rachaduras acentuadas (resultado considerado satisfatório, p. 3). Assentamento com chapa 3/8" chumbada com graute e chapa tipo meia-lua fixada no pilar de concreto, comportando até cinco varas (p. 3).

6Principais achados

Os itens abaixo são afirmações da fonte, não validações da curadoria

  • O número de peças estruturais de sustentação da cobertura é de 55 unidades, com 100% afetadas por alguma patologia; cerca de 55% apresentaram mais de uma patologia; a maior parte das ocorrências concentra-se na área posterior da obra (cerca de 21 colmos), local mais úmido pela vegetação sobreposta (p. 4).
  • Fissuras: ocorrem em 100% das peças; em 98% das peças o tipo é o de fissura longa (ultrapassa a divisão do nó), em algumas peças em todo o comprimento; fissuras curtas ocorrem em todas as peças com fissuras longas, com exceção de uma peça (p. 4). Causa atribuída: exposição às intempéries (vento, umidade, luz solar).
  • Fotodegradação: 55 casos (100% das peças), com perda de pigmento e perda de epiderme para textura áspera; as partes com maior incidência solar são as mais afetadas; acabamento original à base de selador e verniz, com vida limitada (p. 4).
  • Fungos: identificados em todas as peças (manchas acinzentadas, de claras a escuras, circulares e descontínuas); não foi detectado comprometimento pela incidência dos fungos, mas a ausência de manutenção implica agravamento para fungos apodrecedores e perda de resistência; 2 peças sujeitas a umidade e sol excessivos já se encontram comprometidas, sustentando-se apenas pela área concretada, com substituição recomendada em caráter emergencial (p. 4-5).
  • Colonização de insetos: presença de nichos de maribondos em 4 peças, sem impacto estrutural, minimizável com limpeza regular (p. 5).
  • Conexões: 2 problemas de conexão por execução imperfeita da boca de pescado, sem sinais aparentes de comprometimento; oxidação dos parafusos nas ligações em 100% das peças, quando não danificados (quebrados) (p. 4).
  • Cobertura: queda do telhamento na lateral esquerda da nave por acúmulo de folhas e umidade, expondo bambus da estrutura às intempéries — intervenção urgente recomendada para evitar perda de resistência de outras peças (p. 3).
  • Causas prováveis enunciadas: exposição ao sol e chuva, umidade e falta de manutenção (resumo, p. 1); manutenção convencional (a cada 6 meses a 1 ano) não era realizada — a manutenção era feita pelos próprios condôminos (p. 4).
  • Recomendações: intervenção com substituição e/ou reparo conforme a gravidade; braçadeiras para fissuras (impedem o movimento radial dos tecidos e a ampliação da fissura) e calafetagem para fissuras longas; lixamento e pintura com Stain ou verniz para restabelecer a proteção; limpeza e escovação das peças antes do uso e aplicação de verniz com reaplicação periódica (p. 3-5).
  • Conclusão: necessidade urgente de intervenção na obra, sob pena de colapso de peças com função estruturante para a cobertura (p. 5).

7Avaliação crítica

Estudo de caso com método adequado ao objeto (inspeção não destrutiva em obra em uso), mas limitado à avaliação visual e táctil, sem ensaios laboratoriais — limitação declarada pelo autor. A espécie é identificada apenas como Guadua sp., com base em estudos de Graciano & Filgueiras (2015) e relatório não publicado (p. 2). A ausência de norma específica de bambu levou ao uso da NBR 5674:2024 e de procedimentos orientados à madeira, o que é razoável, mas não substitui critérios específicos de bambu-colmo. O gráfico de patologias (Gráfico 1) não é reproduzido com a numeração completa por tipo no texto, que fornece apenas totais parciais. Nota crítica de curadoria: as coordenadas registradas na fonte ("Longitude 9°57'33.9"S e Latitude 67°51'28.6"W", p. 2) apresentam os rótulos de latitude/longitude aparentemente invertidos — o valor com S é latitude e o com W é longitude. O valor documental é alto: registro longitudinal raro de obra real em uso na Amazônia, conectando manejo, tratamento (InKabor 5%), detalhamento construtivo e ausência de manutenção ao desempenho após ~11 anos.

8Inserção no estado da arte

O trabalho insere-se na literatura de patologias e durabilidade de estruturas de bambu, dialogando com Mesquita Júnior (2019, estudo da OCA/SINPRO) e Hidalgo (2003). Complementa a ficha do CONTECC 2025 sobre espécies nativas (Coreia et al.), que cita o mesmo quiosque como exemplo de aplicabilidade local — aqui visto pelo lado da degradação. Traz evidência de campo que tensiona a promessa de durabilidade: obra com bambu nativo tratado (InKabor 5%) atingiu 100% de incidência de patologias após ~11 anos sem manutenção programada, o que reforça no Acervo a tese de que preservação e proteção (tratamento, detalhamento, manutenção) são indissociáveis do desempenho — agenda dos Cadernos 1, 2 e 4, e conexa à ACV do bambu artesanal do Acre (Araujo et al., 2025) e ao levantamento de coleobrocas em Bambusa sp. (Oliveira, Silva e Garlet, 2023).

Relações

Conexão TTR — evidência direta: patologias em obra real de bambu no território de atuação do Acervo (Rio Branco-AC). A fonte documenta, em escala 1:1, os modos de degradação (fissuras, fotodegradação, fungos, insetos, conexões) que os processos de tratamento e proteção do Acervo visam prevenir, e associa a degradação à ausência de manutenção programada — não ao material em si.

Nota de proveniência: ficha elaborada a partir da leitura integral do PDF (hash SHA-256 5bacbf450b3c2eb593933e77fc323797f817b7ebf17d3470d8ca0dbcf8377de9; 6 páginas), com extração integral de texto e metadados catalográficos preservados em documentação privada do acervo. Nenhum dado foi acrescentado por inferência: informações ausentes da fonte estão registradas como "não declarado na fonte".

Ficha: Cordero (1990) — Casa de painéis de bambu-argamassa (histórico)

Cordero · EESC-USP · 1990 · tde-25032026-113412

em-revisao-documentalficha-academica9 seções
1 Dados gerais2 Estrutura e organização3 Problema e perguntas de pesquisa4 Referencial teórico5 Metodologia6 Principais achados7 Avaliação crítica8 Inserção no estado da arte· Relações
Síntese

Dissertação histórica (EESC-USP, 1990; digitalizada em 2026) que desenvolve e ensaia um sistema construtivo de painéis de bambu-argamassa para habitação de baixa renda. Foram ensaiadas 16 vigas de bambu-argamassa (3 x 20 x 120 cm) com régua de Bambusa gigantea, tratamentos CCA, Pentox e frio asfalto; a impermeabilização com frio asfalto deu a menor absorção de água (2,3% vs. 3,8% da testemunha, p. 70) e o melhor desempenho em flexão; a conclusão (p. 112) aponta o sistema como alternativa viável. Scan com OCR imperfeito — trechos ilegíveis marcados.

1Dados gerais

CampoDado
AutorValentin Mamani Cordero
InstituiçãoUSP — EESC, Departamento de Arquitetura e Planejamento
Ano1990 (digitalização 2026)
TipoDissertação de mestrado (histórica digitalizada)
TítuloCasa de painéis de bambu-argamassa
DOI10.11606/D.18.1990.tde-25032026-113412
Páginas154 (scan)
ObservaçãoOCR imperfeito; trechos marcados como ilegíveis

2Estrutura e organização

Introdução ao problema habitacional; bambu como material de construção; sistema bambu-argamassa (painéis, vigas); ensaios de absorção, intemperismo, flexão e desempenho térmico; conclusão sobre viabilidade para habitação de baixa renda.

3Problema e perguntas de pesquisa

É viável construir habitação de baixa renda com painéis de bambu-argamassa? Qual o desempenho de diferentes tratamentos (CCA, Pentox, frio asfalto) na durabilidade e nas propriedades mecânicas?

4Referencial teórico

  • Bambu como material construtivo;
  • Bambu-cimento / bambu-argamassa;
  • Tratamentos preservativos e impermeabilizantes;
  • Habitação de interesse social.

5Metodologia

Fabricação e ensaio de 16 vigas de bambu-argamassa (3 x 20 x 120 cm) com régua de Bambusa gigantea; tratamentos: CCA, Pentox e frio asfalto; ensaios de absorção de água, intemperismo, flexão e desempenho térmico.

6Principais achados

Os itens abaixo são afirmações da fonte, não validações da curadoria.

  • Impermeabilização com frio asfalto: menor absorção de água (2,3% vs. 3,8% da testemunha, p. 70) e melhor desempenho em flexão;
  • Sistema construtivo bambu-argamassa indicado como alternativa viável para habitação de baixa renda (p. 112).

7Avaliação crítica

Potencialidades:

  • Documento histórico do campo (1990) que antecipa a discussão de painéis bambu-cimento;
  • Ensaio comparativo de tratamentos (CCA, Pentox, frio asfalto).

Limitações:

  • Scan com OCR imperfeito — parte dos dados numéricos não legível;
  • Métodos e normas da época (1990) — não equivalentes aos atuais.

8Inserção no estado da arte

Registro histórico fundamental para o eixo de bambu estrutural: documenta a trajetória dos painéis bambu-cimento no Brasil, antecedendo a literatura recente (RMAT 2024, bioconcretos). Conexão TTR: analogia-tecnica (painéis bambu-argamassa vs. painéis atuais do Acervo).

Relações

  • Conexão com tecnologias do Acervo (TTR): analogia-tecnica (painéis de bambu-argamassa; histórico que precede os bioconcretos atuais).
  • Proveniência: download 2026-07-31 via teses USP; 154 páginas (scan) conferidas; hash 41baaf2b…; operação de fichamento curatorial (BAMBU-COMP-006; tipo historico).

Tratamento térmico de Dendrocalamus asper para BLC — Costa (2015)

ausente-na-fonte

em-revisao-documentalficha-academica8 seções
1 Identificação2 Objetivo3 Material e Métodos4 Resultados5 Observações relevantes6 Conclusões da autora7 Principais referências citadas8 Palavras-chave

Referência completa: COSTA, Amanda Monteiro. **Tratamento térmico de Dendrocalamus asper para confecção de Bambu Laminado Colado (BLC)**. 2015. 37 f. Trabalho de conclusão de curso (Graduação em Engenharia Florestal) — Universidade de Brasília, Brasília, 2015.

O original integral foi preservado na área privada do Acervo. A fonte não apresenta DOI, ISBN ou Handle, mas contém autoria, instituição, natureza acadêmica e ano verificáveis.

1Identificação

CampoDescrição
AutoraAmanda Monteiro Costa
OrientadorProf. Dr. Alexandre Florian da Costa
CoorientadorDr. Fernando Nunes Gouveia (LPF/SFB)
InstituiçãoUniversidade de Brasília (UnB) — Faculdade de Tecnologia, Departamento de Engenharia Florestal
TipoTrabalho de Conclusão de Curso (Graduação em Engenharia Florestal)
Ano2015
LocalBrasília-DF
Nº de páginas37

2Objetivo

Avaliar as propriedades físico-mecânicas da espécie Dendrocalamus asper (Schult. & Schult.) tratada termicamente na forma de taliscas e de Bambu Laminado Colado (BLC).

3Material e Métodos

3.1. Material vegetal

  • Espécie: Dendrocalamus asper (bambu gigante/balde)
  • Idade dos colmos: aproximadamente 3 anos
  • Origem: estoque do CPAB (Centro de Pesquisa Aplicada de Bambu e Fibras Naturais — Universidade de Brasília)
  • Corpos de prova: 350 taliscas com dimensões 2,0 cm (largura) × 0,8 cm (espessura) × 49 cm (comprimento)

3.2. Locais de execução

  • Laboratório de Produtos Florestais (LPF) — Serviço Florestal Brasileiro (SFB)
  • Centro de Pesquisa Aplicada de Bambu e Fibras Naturais (CPAB) — Universidade de Brasília

3.3. Tratamentos térmicos

TratamentoTemperaturaTempo
A150 °C2 h
B150 °C4 h
C180 °C2 h
D180 °C4 h
T (Testemunha)—sem tratamento
  • Estufa: Fabbe Primar, com ventilação forçada de ar
  • Termopares: tipo K, ligados a multímetro digital Bratec MD-380
  • Resfriamento: 24 h dentro da estufa após o tratamento
  • Climatização: 20 ± 3 °C e 65 ± 5% de UR até massa constante

3.4. Ensaios realizados

  • Massa específica básica — submersão em água por 15 dias; volume verde com paquímetro digital Mitutoyo; massa seca em estufa Fanem a 100 °C até massa constante.
  • Perda de massa — aferição antes e após tratamento; regra de três simples.
  • Flexão estática (COPANT 555/73) — máquina Instron; vão livre: 12 cm (taliscas), 45,5 cm (BLC); determinação de MOE (Módulo de Elasticidade) e MOR (Módulo de Ruptura).
  • Ondas de tensão (não destrutivo) — Stress Wave Timer Metriguard 239A; 3 medições por amostra no sentido longitudinal; cálculo do MOEd (Módulo de Elasticidade Dinâmico).
  • Confecção dos BLCs — 4 camadas; adesivo poliuretano TekBond (150 g/m²); prensa artesanal manual por 24 h; 10 amostras/tratamento.

3.5. Análise estatística

  • Software: SPSS n. 13
  • Testes: ANOVA; Tukey (comparação entre tratamentos); Dunnett (comparação com testemunha)
  • Nível de significância: 5%
  • Regressão: MOEd (Stress Wave) × MOE e MOR estáticos

4Resultados

4.1. Massa específica básica

  • Média: 0,51 g/cm³
  • Classificação: material leve
  • Comparação: próxima a Ferreira (2014) — 0,50–0,55 g/cm³; inferior a Beraldo & Rivero (2003) — 0,58–0,79 g/cm³

4.2. Perda de massa

TratamentoMassa antes (g)Massa após (g)Perda (%)Grupo
A (150 °C/2h)73,9965,4911,47b
B (150 °C/4h)72,5363,9411,85b
C (180 °C/2h)70,3560,5213,98ab
D (180 °C/4h)73,5762,6314,86c
  • A perda de massa foi significativa entre os tratamentos (Tukey, 5%).
  • Temperatura e tempo afetaram a perda; 180 °C produziu as maiores perdas.

4.3. MOE (Módulo de Elasticidade) — Flexão Estática

T (Testemunha)15.6832.367,0a

\* Diferiu significativamente da testemunha (Dunnett, 5%).

O tratamento D (180 °C/4h) piorou as propriedades mecânicas.

BLC

4.4. MOR (Módulo de Ruptura)

Taliscas

A (150 °C/2h)171,337,8a
B (150 °C/4h)198,537,4a

\* Diferiram da testemunha (pioraram).

BLC

TratamentoMOR (MPa)Desvio PadrãoGrupo estatístico
A (150 °C/2h)80,7224,8a
B (150 °C/4h)59,8010,1b \*

\* A tabela da fonte marca B, C e D como diferentes da testemunha pelo teste de Dunnett, embora o texto imediatamente anterior diga que esses tratamentos não diferiram da testemunha. A ficha preserva essa inconsistência interna. O tratamento A apresentou o maior valor médio e grupo Tukey distinto, mas não recebeu a marca de Dunnett na tabela.

4.5. MOEd (Módulo de Elasticidade Dinâmico)

  • Taliscas: comportamento similar ao MOE estático; tratamento D piorou as propriedades.
  • BLC: não houve diferenças estatísticas significativas entre os tratamentos.
  • Coeficiente informado nos gráficos como R:
  • Taliscas: R = 0,558
  • BLC: R = 0,0578 — associação muito baixa

A fonte interpreta esses valores como percentuais de “confiabilidade”. A ficha não os converte em R² porque os gráficos os rotulam apenas como R.

4.6. Efeito Temperatura × Tempo

  • A temperatura teve maior influência que o tempo de tratamento nas propriedades físico-mecânicas (corroborando Oliveira 2012 e Ferreira 2014).
  • Para as taliscas, o fator tempo não foi significativo para MOE e MOR.
  • Para o BLC, houve diferença significativa entre tempo e testemunha no MOE.

5Observações relevantes

  • Grande parte dos BLCs rompeu na linha de cola durante a flexão estática, indicando falha no processo de colagem (prensa artesanal sem controle de pressão).
  • O MOEd mostrou baixa correlação com o MOE estático, especialmente para o BLC (R² = 5,7%), sugerindo que o Stress Wave Timer não foi um bom preditor para este material.

6Conclusões da autora

  • A temperatura foi a variável que mais afetou o tratamento térmico, tanto em taliscas quanto no BLC.
  • Para as taliscas, o tratamento térmico não se mostrou eficiente para aumento da resistência à flexão estática.
  • A autora conclui que o tratamento térmico melhorou as propriedades mecânicas dos BLCs e identifica A (150 °C durante 2 horas) como o melhor tratamento. A leitura deve considerar a inconsistência estatística registrada na seção 4.4 e as rupturas observadas na linha de cola.
  • Sugestões:
  • Maior controle da pressão na confecção dos BLCs para minimizar rompimentos na linha de cola.
  • Realização de testes de durabilidade (apodrecimento acelerado) para avaliar resistência a agentes degradadores.

7Principais referências citadas

  • FERREIRA, L. M. C. (2014) — Design de Móveis e Bambu Laminado Colado: Consideração ao tratamento térmico — base comparativa central do estudo.
  • BERALDO, A. L. & RIVERO, L. A. (2003) — Bambu Laminado Colado (BLC) — referência para valores de MOE (18.400 MPa) e massa específica.
  • BRITO, F. M. S. (2013) — Efeito da termorretificação nas propriedades tecnológicas do bambu.
  • COLLA, W. A. (2010) — Tratamento térmico em Dendrocalamus giganteus.
  • OLIVEIRA (2012) — Tratamento térmico em Bambusa tuldoides (160–200 °C).

8Palavras-chave

Tratamento térmico; Dendrocalamus asper; taliscas; Bambu Laminado Colado (BLC); Módulo de Elasticidade (MOE); Módulo de Ruptura (MOR); Módulo de Elasticidade Dinâmico (MOEd); ondas de tensão; flexão estática.

Revisão documental: 14 de julho de 2026. Resultados, tabelas e conclusões confrontados com o original integral. A ausência de identificador persistente não impede a identificação deste trabalho acadêmico.

Circular Embrapa 65 — produção de extrato pirolenhoso

Campos · 2007 · Embrapa Clima Temperado, Circular Técnica 65, ISSN 1981-5999

em-revisao-documentaldocumento-institucional8 seções
1 Dados gerais2 Estrutura e organização3 Problema e finalidade4 Referencial técnico5 Procedimento descrito6 Pontos centrais7 Avaliação crítica8 Uso no acervo

Natureza: Documento técnico institucional de orientação. Não é ensaio de eficácia de um produto específico.

1Dados gerais

Ângela Diniz Campos; Embrapa Clima Temperado; Circular Técnica 65; Pelotas, dezembro de 2007; ISSN 1981-5999; 8 páginas.

2Estrutura e organização

Apresenta origem do condensado, riscos, forno e coleta, temperatura, repouso, separação e recomendações de qualidade.

3Problema e finalidade

Orienta produção de extrato com menor contaminação por alcatrão para possível uso agrícola.

4Referencial técnico

Resume literatura e prática de carbonização, composição do condensado e histórico de uso.

5Procedimento descrito

Discute adaptação de fornos, controle de coleta, condensação, decantação e separação de frações.

6Pontos centrais

  • O condensado bruto contém água e numerosos compostos.
  • Alcatrão e benzopirenos são riscos relevantes.
  • Temperatura de coleta e separação condicionam a qualidade.
  • O documento recomenda rigor técnico e cuidado no manuseio.

7Avaliação crítica

A circular não demonstra segurança ou eficácia agronômica de qualquer extrato. Recomendações de 2007 também devem ser confrontadas com regulação e evidência atuais.

8Uso no acervo

É referência de processo e segurança para interpretar trabalhos com ácido pirolenhoso, sem servir como certificado ambiental ou sanitário.

Referência ABNT: CAMPOS, Ângela Diniz. Técnicas para produção de extrato pirolenhoso para uso agrícola. Pelotas: Embrapa Clima Temperado, 2007. 8 p. (Circular Técnica, 65). ISSN 1981-5999.

Editorial note — preserved instruments

The two following sections — Evidence map (summary) and Timeline (1990–2025) — are EDA instruments preserved in full. They provide historical traceability and an independent thematic count (total 51 in the Evidence Map). They are not the scientific corpus (54 records with integral source verified); they constitute instruments that converse with Part 4 and with the transition to the technical evidence (§2–§8). They remain positioned between the editorial opening and technical §2, kept intact.

Curatorial registration note (2026-08-01)

Curatorial registration note (2026-08-01): the registration divergences pointed out in previous versions of this document were resolved — fabricated records were removed from the drawer (Silva 2011 "conservação"; Wang 2020 with nonexistent DOI) and the LCA duplicate was reconciled (Araujo 2025), with the material preserved in private backup. Since then, the drawer operates with a single record per work; see correction log (private file).

Confidence levels (curatorial scale, inspired by GRADE, without formal adoption — curator's decision): High confidence — multiple independent and convergent records; Moderate confidence — consistent evidence, but limited in number, scope or nature (bench scale, exploration or documentary record); Low confidence — few sources or sources of fragile nature; Promising hypothesis — expressive bench-scale performance awaiting scale and standards validation; Insufficient evidence — the drawer does not contain a documentary basis for the claim (e.g.: normative conformity of pyroligneous acid, long-term field efficacy, automatic sustainability).

2Bamboo material: properties, heat treatment and preservation

2.1. Physical and mechanical properties of the culm

The record of Adier et al. (2023) — a systematic review conducted according to PRISMA guidelines over articles from 2010–2023 in the Scopus and Web of Science databases — compiles property ranges of the most studied species: tensile strength of Guadua angustifolia averaging 226 MPa, Phyllostachys edulis between 147 and 423 MPa, compressive strength parallel to the fibers of G. angustifolia of up to 220 MPa and density between 500 and 1,100 kg/m³. The record of Gutiérrez-González and Takeuchi-Tam (2014) qualifies the structural use of Colombian guadua: in the usual service moisture range (approximately 12% to 19%), the tensile strength parallel to the fibers showed no relevant variation attributable to moisture; more important variations occurred below the hygroscopic equilibrium and above the fiber saturation point. The record of Oliveira et al. (2025) registers, for Dendrocalamus strictus (solid bamboo, 3-to-5-year-old culms, tests per NBR 16828-2), average strengths of 68.83 MPa in compression parallel and about 123.5 MPa in tension parallel, with an average moisture content of 15.29% — values from the source itself, obtained with minimal sampling (one specimen per condition). The CONTECC (2025) record on native species compares the established species (G. angustifolia, Dendrocalamus giganteus) with Amazonian natives (Guadua weberbaueri, Guadua spp.), concluding a structural and non-structural potential conditioned on the absence of Brazilian standardization, on the shortage of applied research and on the need for preservative treatments.

2.2. Heat treatment: steam, liquid media and oven

The record on high-temperature saturated steam in moso bamboo (Wang et al., 2020) shows that treating fresh culms at 140–180 °C for 10–30 min reduced the equilibrium moisture, above all by degradation of hemicelluloses, but produced a trade-off between dimensional stability and mechanical strength: at 180 °C for 30 min, MOR and MOE fell approximately 47% and 20% relative to the control; the authors indicated 160 °C/30 min or 180 °C/10 min as promising conditions to balance moisture reduction and mechanical preservation.

The record of Chung and Wang (2017) examines peeling of the epidermis and steam treatment at 120 °C for 6 h on culms of Phyllostachys makinoi and P. pubescens: under the tested conditions, the two factors altered composition, density, equilibrium moisture, water absorption, dimensional stability and flexural strength. The record on heat treatment in polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) (Zhang et al., 2020) shows that moso bamboo strips heated for 3 h in PDMS at 120–210 °C reduced equilibrium moisture, swelling and wettability, with reduction of mechanical properties under part of the conditions; the record notes that the work does not prove environmental equivalence with treatments without synthetic polymers.

In a conventional oven, the record of Costa (2015) evaluated slats of Dendrocalamus asper (culms of approximately 3 years) at 150 and 180 °C for 2 and 4 h, with the making of 4-layer BLC: mass loss varied from 11.47% (150 °C/2 h) to 14.86% (180 °C/4 h); in the BLC, the 150 °C/2 h treatment raised the MOE (11,794 MPa) relative to the control (9,387 MPa), while 180 °C/4 h worsened the mechanical properties (MOE 8,996 MPa); on slats, the best average MOR was that of 150 °C/4 h (198.5 MPa). The record of Oliveira et al. (2025), with a 3×3 factorial design (160–200 °C; 1–2 h) on D. strictus, concluded that the adopted ranges had little effect on the parallel compressive and tensile strengths (control: 64.42 and 126.76 MPa) and that the treatment delayed borer attack — with the explicit caveat of minimal sampling and the absence of analysis of variance. The record on bamboo scrimber (Shangguan et al., 2016) warns about the specificity of composites: in bundles of Neosinocalamus affinis impregnated with phenol-formaldehyde resin (average density of 1.22 g/cm³) and heated for 2 h between 50 and 230 °C, compressive strength reached a maximum around 170 °C, attributed by the authors to additional curing of the adhesive, and higher temperatures began to degrade performance.

2.3. Preservative treatment and chemical modification

The thesis of Gauss (2020) quantifies boron (DOT) retention in D. asper: 14.79 kg/m³ with a 5% solution and 21.79 kg/m³ at 8%, above the AWPA recommendations (2.7 kg/m³) and IS 401:2001 (5 kg/m³) for interior use; the tannin/hexamine/boron treatment (T10HB5) maintained low mass loss from fungi even after leaching (7.58% for Pycnoporus sanguineus and 1.35% for Gloeophyllum trabeum, versus 15.03% and 10.52% for the leached reference). The lecture of Gauss (2023) is a record of teaching material (12 pages) that organizes the preservation vocabulary — passive and active methods, diffusion/capillarity versus pressurized processes, Boucherie, autoclave — and, as the record itself registers, should not be treated as a literal quotation of the speaker nor as evidence of performance.

2.4. Pyroligneous extract and organic routes

The Embrapa Technical Circular 65 (2007) is a process reference: it guides the production of the extract with less tar contamination, warns about the risks of tar and benzopyrenes and, as the record registers, does not demonstrate the safety or efficacy of any extract. The experimental records on pyroligneous acid present a mixed picture, but none demonstrates conformity. The record of Silva (2011) documents a 20-week test with BLC in dilutions of 10%, 20% and 30%: 46.67% of the specimens remained intact, 10.48% had signs of penetration (ten of the eleven attacked in the node region), and there was no statistical difference that would support the efficacy of one dilution over the others or over the control — the author himself concludes that the test did not allow demonstrating durability. The record of Matsuoka and Beraldo (2014), with machined slats of D. giganteus immersed in heated solutions (pure product and dilutions from 5% to 30%, 15 to 180 min) and soil exposure at 80% of water-holding capacity, registers that mass loss and ultrasound did not allow distinguishing the effects of the soil, the concentration or the immersion time, without conclusive fungicidal efficacy. The record of Laroque (2022) — a study on Pinus elliottii, not bamboo — is the explicit methodological counterpoint: the raw liquid reduced losses from fungi (26.07% in the control to 14.09% in autoclave and 10.47% in immersion) and from termites (3.68% to 0.83% and 1.31%), but all conditions exceeded the 3% limit adopted by the author, who did not consider the raw preservative adequate by the reference standard. The record of Martins (2017) is an in vitro screening: Trametes versicolor still grew 0.85 cm in the 0.5% condition cited in the conclusion; there was no growth of Neolentinus lepideus on the treated plates; the author himself recommends additional tests to distinguish a fungicidal from a fungistatic effect. The record of Pimentel's bi-oil treatment (s.d.) is exploratory evidence: baths of rapeseed oil (hot) and linseed oil (cold) caused cracks in most D. giganteus compression samples (only one of the six did not crack), and the author herself declares that analyses are lacking.

2.5. State of this axis

Moderate confidence (high for the thermal window; insufficient evidence for pyroligneous conformity). The sources support that (i) heat treatment improves dimensional stability and reduces attractiveness to insects, but has an operational window: above a certain severity (180 °C/4 h in an oven in Costa 2015; 180 °C/30 min in steam in Wang et al. 2020; from 170 °C in the scrimber) the mechanical properties fall; and (ii) pyroligneous acid reduces xylophage and fungus activity in laboratory tests, but no record demonstrates conformity as a preservative by standard — the only one that applied a normative criterion (Laroque 2022, in pine) rejected the raw product. The records do not support the equivalence of pyroligneous acid to commercial preservatives, nor long-term field efficacy: the only controlled test in bamboo (Silva 2011) found no statistical difference, and the only normative criterion applied (Laroque 2022, in pine) rejected the product (see section 8).

3Industrial transformation: densification, laminates, CLB and panels

3.1. Densification

The thesis of Sá (2022) characterized laminated (non-densified) D. asper elements and elements densified with bark (DC) and without bark (DS), by thermo-hydraulic press at 140 °C, 5 MPa for 15 min: the apparent density went from 0.79 to 0.92–0.99 g/cm³, with emphasis on the DC group (average MOR of approximately 312 MPa; MOE of 31.44 GPa), and the raw-material yield rose from 28% (lamination) to 46% (densification with rectification); the recorded cost is the greater water absorption and radial swelling, mitigated when the bark is kept. The thesis of Godoy Júnior (2024) tested alkaline delignification (NaOH 2.5 mol/L + Na₂SO₃ 0.4 mol/L at 25 °C and 100 °C), two drying methods (oven at 100 °C and ambient at 25 °C) and thermo-mechanical densification at 160 °C up to 50% thickness reduction: the pretreatment reduced the required compressive stress (17 MPa in the reference to 7–13.4 MPa; the boiled and ambient-dried group required only 40% of the stress of the untreated one), but degraded the final mechanical properties (MOR −29% to −46%; MOE −18% to −33%), leading the author to conclude that the concentration of alkaline solution in an open system with 50% densification is not sufficient for adequate densification.

3.2. Glued laminate and panels

The thesis of Reghin Filho (2018) produced artisanal BLC of D. giganteus with castor-oil-based polyurethane adhesive: apparent density of 0.79 g/cm³, average compressive strength parallel of 74.67 MPa and record of productive obstacles (lack of equipment, standardization, labor and commercial supply) and, in the opinion survey, of the need for greater technical-scientific dissemination. The record of Rusch et al. (2019) compared panels of P. aurea and D. asper by glued lamination and thermo-mechanical process: apparent density between 0.75 and 0.79 g/cm³, equilibrium moisture between 7.83% and 10.42%, higher mechanical values in the thermo-mechanical process — for D. asper, MOR of 146.8 MPa, shear of 6.36 MPa and Janka hardness of 3,852 N; for P. aurea, the maximum MOE cited of 19,603 MPa. The thesis of Tarverdi (2024) investigated flattened-densified bamboo panels of D. asper (3-year-old culms) with castor-oil-based polyurethane adhesive and pressing at 170 °C: the parallel group with internal faces glued (P IN-IN) presented the best flexural results (MOR 239.24 MPa; MOE 25,032 MPa) and lower water absorption (4.47% in 24 h), evidencing lamina orientation as the determining factor. The thesis of Martins (2021) analyzes the industrialization of glued laminated bamboo (BaLC) in Brazil: seven processing stages (species → culms → slat cutting → immunization → drying/storage → gluing → tests/prototypes), yield of about 30% of the culm into slats, PVA adhesives (interior use) and MUF/RF (exterior/structural), absence of commercial plantations, cost of the imported adhesive, lack of a specific standard for BaLC and PNMCB not regulated.

3.3. Engineered bamboo and CLB

The thesis of Alves (2025) characterizes the global engineered structural bamboo industry — over 635 websites investigated, 20 companies selected, with strong concentration in China (13) — and presents a systematic review on cross-laminated bamboo (CLB): basis in bamboo scrimber, lamellae of 6.25–20 mm, 3–8 layers, PUR/RF/PRF/MUF adhesives, cold press 0.2–5 MPa. According to the record, CLB shows superior performance to CLT in flexure, compression and transverse shear, but faces standardization gaps, specific standards and durability data.

3.4. Digital fabrication and historical antecedents

The thesis of Ruggiero (2021) validates by simulation (Karamba 3D) a laminated bamboo reticular structure with three sections (10×3.8 / 10×7.6 / 15.2×7.6 cm; masses of 445 / 892 / 1,355 kg; maximum displacements of 13.94 / 3.76 / 1.71 cm), without collapse in any option, relating digital fabrication to quality control and reproducibility — simulation result, without a constructed counterpart. The thesis of Cordero (1990) is the historical antecedent of the axis (EESC-USP, digitized in 2026, scan with imperfect OCR): 16 bamboo-mortar beams (3 × 20 × 120 cm) with Bambusa gigantea reinforcing and CCA, Pentox and cold asphalt treatments; waterproofing with cold asphalt gave the lowest water absorption (2.3% versus 3.8% of the control) and the best flexural performance, concluding feasibility for low-income housing.

3.5. State of this axis

Moderate confidence (bench-scale performance; insufficient evidence for industrial scale). The records support that densification raises density and flexural strength (Sá 2022), that lamina orientation and bark retention condition panel performance (Tarverdi 2024; Sá 2022) and that CLB is a material with promising performance, still without its own standards (Alves 2025). The axis does not support Brazilian industrial-scale validation: the studies are bench or pilot scale (Reghin, Rusch, Tarverdi, Sá), and the Martins (2021) record documents structural barriers (~30% yield, imported adhesive, absence of a standard for BaLC). The negative result of Godoy Júnior's (2024) alkaline pretreatment is an important counterpoint to delignification routes in open systems.

4Composites and derived materials (bioconcrete, ashes, pulp, residues)

4.1. Composites with industrial residues

The thesis of Santos (2020) produced isophthalic unsaturated polyester matrix composites with Bambusa vulgaris fibers (15 and 30 mm, in natura and treated with NaOH 5% for 2 h) and Amazonian industrial residues (red mud from Hydro Alunorte/Barcarena, copper flotation residue from VALE/Mina do Sossego and secondary kaolin residue from Imerys Rio Capim Caulim), by hand lay-up and pressing. According to the record, the best results were: tensile of 41.07 MPa (hybrid 20% kaolin/3% treated 15 mm fibers), flexural of 150.94 MPa (treated 30 mm fibers), impact of 38.56 kJ/m² (hybrid) and HB classification in the horizontal flammability test (ASTM D635-10).

4.2. Ashes and bioconcretes

The thesis of Mendonça (2018) investigated the partial replacement of Portland cement by bamboo ashes: the B. vulgaris culm ash calcined at 600 °C obtained a 28-day performance index with cement higher than required by NBR 12653 (ABNT 2014), with a compressive strength gain of the mortars between 10 and 15% and more expressive calcium hydroxide consumption with 10% replacement. The record of Gangorra et al. (2024) characterized bioconcretes with fine bamboo particles (< 1.18 mm) replacing 0%, 5%, 10% and 13% of the volume of bio-aggregates (ternary cementitious matrix with 35% fly ash and 20% rice husk ash; bio-aggregates pretreated with calcium hydroxide): the mix with 13% fines had greater compaction, lower capillary absorption (up to 45.66% lower in 48 h) and higher 28-day compressive strength (10.42 MPa; +15.27% in strength and +5.90% in modulus versus the reference), with greater drying shrinkage.

4.3. Cellulosic pulp

The thesis of Santos (2023) characterized the biomass of four Bambusa species (B. vulgaris var. vittata, B. tuldoides, B. oldhamii and B. nutans) and subjected chips to kraft pulping at eight active alkali charges (11% to 25%): estimated screened yield of 50.3–52.5% (kappa 18) and 57.0–59.3% (kappa 58), with B. nutans and B. vulgaris superior (lower alkali charge for the same kappa) and B. tuldoides advised against; active alkali charges below 15% can cause lignin reprecipitation, and the 11% charge was fully consumed during pulping. The author situates the work in the bio-based economy, indicating bamboo as an alternative non-wood long fiber for the Brazilian pulp industry.

4.4. Bioactives, flow chemistry and energy conversion

The record of Sola et al. (2023) registers the in vitro antibacterial potential of hydroalcoholic extracts of leaves and culms of Guadua aff. lynnclarkiae (Western Amazon): only the leaves had a bactericidal effect for the three tested strains (MBC from 1.55 to 25 mg/ml), while the culms had bacteriostatic action (MIC from 1.55 to 6.25 mg/ml), with bactericidal action at 6.25 mg/ml only for Staphylococcus aureus. The record itself classifies the study as technical analogy with the pyroligneous line (liquid biomass extracts with reported biological activity), without endorsement of therapeutic claims by the curatorship. The capillary bamboo microreactor patent (BR 102019003286-3 B1, Faculdades Católicas) documents the use of the vascular channels of bamboo as a flow reactor functionalized with copper and palladium, with declared yields of 50% to 95% in the examples and unidentified species — patent data, without independent replication. The rocket stove record (Stefanditya et al., 2023) is an exclusively computational result: the addition of 30 mm of ceramic fiber raised the temperature under the pot from 374.91 °C to 452.94 °C in CFD simulation, without comparative prototype, thermal efficiency test or emissions measurement. The review of Hernández-Mena et al. (2024) situates the set: neotropical woody bamboos as biomass for bioproducts and bioenergy, with Brazil gathering 258 described species, of which 165 woody, and knowledge fragmented among botany, ecology, energy and materials.

4.5. State of this axis

Low to moderate confidence (all materials characterized at laboratory scale). The records support the reuse of processing residues in cementitious and polymeric matrices with point performance gains (Mendonça 2018; Gangorra et al. 2024; Santos 2020), the potential of bamboo as a non-wood long fiber for pulp (Santos 2023) and the biological activity of extracts in in vitro tests (Sola et al. 2023). The axis does not support: cement replacement without standard durability tests at scale; therapeutic implications of extracts; real thermal performance of stoves (simulation result). All materials were characterized at laboratory scale, without long-duration validation or continuous production.

5Structures and building systems

5.1. Architectural practice and structural systems

The thesis of Bussinger (2024) systematizes the São Paulo architectural production with structural bamboo culm: 16 identified works (2003–2023) and 6 case studies built between 2017 and 2023, analyzed under the axes of architecture, structural system, quality and durability. The record registers the recurrent use of five species of INBAR priority interest, the diversity of connectors (more than one type per structure, without clear correlation with the form), cracks in all culms of all cases and the centrality of moisture-content control, structural redundancy and post-construction inspections for durability.

5.2. Connections

The review of Hong et al. (2019) (Journal of Renewable Materials, v. 7, n. 8) organizes connections for round bamboo structures into two traditional families — interlockings and lashings — and four groups of modern solutions: bolted joints; joints with steel profiles or plates; joints reinforced by filling; and other solutions (polymeric reinforcements, wood components, custom parts). The review treats the connection as a decisive element for safety, durability and spread of the structures, but does not declare a systematic review protocol nor formal search criteria.

5.3. Mixed structures, prestressing and dynamic performance

The record of Puma Alvarez (2014) documents shaking-table tests (1:20 scale) of bamboo prototypes and of a mixed bamboo-reinforced-concrete structure, excited with the Kobe earthquake record and sine waves: the mixed model supported the applied excitations (maximum relative displacement converted to 2.3 cm at the equivalent scale, estimated drift of 7.6/1000), with the article itself declaring that the experiment is not sufficient to establish the safety of real structures with more than two stories. The prestressed bamboo structural element patent (BR PI 1106035-2 B1, UFMG; filed 2011, granted 2022) describes a culm with externally tensioned longitudinal cables: the example reports a lateral displacement of 122 mm under a load of 10.73 kN in a 6 m element with spacers every 2 m, without species identification nor comparative experimental series — as the record registers, the grant protects novelty and inventive activity, but does not certify structural performance for general use.

5.4. Tectonics and constructive culture

The thesis of Santos (2024) analyzes the poetics of the tectonic narrative in three projects with structural bamboo — Ananda House (2015) and The ARC (2021), from the IBUKU office (Bali, Indonesia), and Refúgio das Borboletas, by Helena Ruette (Chapada dos Veadeiros-GO) — applying analytical parameters of tectonics in three relations (site/formal structure, load-bearing system/formal structure, enclosure/formal structure). The record concludes that the tectonic narrative of structural bamboo expresses itself above all through the versatility of the grass, the technical details of the junctions — the Group 2 connection of Widyowijatnoko appears in all three projects — and by a conception process consonant with the constructive culture of the material.

5.5. State of this axis

Moderate confidence (documentation of built practice); insufficient evidence for quantitative full-scale structural validation. The axis is strong in documentation of built practice (Bussinger 2024; Santos 2024) and in experimental exploration (Puma Alvarez 2014), but weak in quantitative full-scale structural validation: the only source with a dynamic test is reduced scale; prestressing exists as a patent, not as verified performance; Ruggiero's (2021) simulations have no constructed counterpart. The records support that the durability of the works depends more on design — moisture control, structural redundancy, maintenance — than on a single treatment, converging with the evidence of pathologies in section 6.

6Pests, durability and protection

6.1. Xylophagous insects

The record of Oliveira, Silva and Garlet (2023) registers an entomological survey in a Bambusa sp. planting in Alta Floresta-MT (Southern Amazon), with 16 ethanolic traps between August 2016 and July 2017: 2,144 individuals, 19 species, in 3 families (Bostrichidae, Cerambycidae and Curculionidae), with Xyleborus affinis as the most frequent species (1,177 individuals) — and the finding that bamboo, being rich in starch, offers little natural resistance to xylophages, requiring treatment. The record of Pena (2013) is comparative, with a distinct host (Banisteriopsis caapi): 2,879 Scolytinae of 68 species and 299 Bostrichidae of five species, with taxonomic and methodological contribution — the record itself warns that it is not evidence of attack, prevention or treatment of bamboo culms.

6.2. Control and management

The thesis of Silveira (2015) brings together experiments on capture and control alternatives of the borer Dinoderus minutus in post-harvest: higher rainfall coincided with higher capture; traps at 2.5 m numerically favored capture, without statistical significance in the corresponding chapter; the thesis provides rearing and capture protocols useful for new studies. The record warns that the results must be read by chapter and do not form a single validation of "sustainable control" by cashew nut shell liquid, electromagnetic exposure or traps.

6.3. Pathologies on site

The record of Afonso (2025) is direct evidence in the Acervo's area of operation: non-destructive visual and tactile inspection (based on ABNT NBR 5674:2024) of the roof structure in native bamboo (Guadua sp.) of the Quiosque do Coco, in Parque do Tucumã, Rio Branco-AC, with about 11 years of construction and absence of scheduled maintenance, found 100% of the 55 structural pieces affected: cracks (100% of pieces, 98% of the long type), photodegradation (100%), staining fungi (100%), 4 pieces with wasp nests and 2 with incorrect connection; the causes pointed out were exposure to sun and rain, moisture and lack of maintenance.

6.4. Moisture and durability

The record of Gutiérrez-González and Takeuchi-Tam (2014) delimits the service range (≈12% to 19% moisture) in which the parallel tensile strength of guadua does not vary relevantly. The record of Oliveira et al. (2025) registers the biological test with D. minutus (21 days of exposure): mass loss from 1.47% in the control to 0.51%, 0.41% and 0.19% at 160 °C for 1 h, 1.5 h and 2 h, respectively — with the declared limitations of few insects and coverage of only the 160 °C temperature. The Bussinger (2024) thesis adds the on-site dimension: cracks in all culms of the studied cases and moisture-content control as a central durability factor.

6.5. State of this axis

Moderate confidence (diagnosis); insufficient evidence for field efficacy of control measures. The records support that xylophage attack is the main biological factor of deterioration of bamboo in post-harvest (richness and abundance documented in the Southern Amazon; bjb-2023-coleobrocas), that heat treatment in moderate ranges delays the attack (Oliveira 2025) and that works without maintenance develop generalized pathologies (Afonso 2025). The axis does not support field efficacy of control by traps, cashew nut shell liquid or electromagnetic exposure as an approved product (Silveira 2015, by chapter), nor equivalence of organic extracts to commercial preservatives. Central gap: absence of long-duration field tests with pyroligneous acid or heat treatment in bamboo.

7Phytoremediation

7.1. Copper and lead in moso bamboo (integral primary sources)

The drawer has come to include the phytoremediation front, with two integral primary source records:

  • The record of Chen et al. (2015) — copper (Cu) in Phyllostachys pubescens (moso): pot experiment (2 months, 0–600 mg/kg Cu) with root BAF between 0.54 and 1.41 and TF between 0.07 and 0.23 (Table 3, p. 4–5); the article concludes that moso is not a hyperaccumulator of Cu; the hydroponics (Table 4) only measures enzymes (SOD/POD/MDA) and proline, without BAF/TF.
  • The record of Liu et al. (2015) — lead (Pb) in P. pubescens (moso): hydroponics (30 days, 0–400 µmol/L Pb) with BCF between 10.97 and 37.64 and TF between 0.07 and 0.37; maximum concentration of 4,282.8 mg/kg in the root (400 µmol/L); all TF < 1 and BCF > 10.

Both are experimental and specific to the test conditions (pot/hydroponics; young seedlings; nutrient solution). They do not constitute a general phytoremediation recommendation, they do not attest performance in real soil and they do not equate to certification. The records register the literal definition of the factors (BAF = tissue/soil; TF = CS/CR, BCF = Cp/Cm) and the nomenclatural note (P. pubescens = synonym of P. edulis, GBIF).

7.2. Pending or private sources (NOT counted as evidence)

The following phytoremediation sources do not integrate this state of the art until confirmation by integral primary source (rule of GOVERNANCA_DOCUMENTAL.md): the Nemenyi (2022) review — private, with divergences to resolve (Zn FT, Pb, Cu 3.04); Bian 2017 (paywall); Liu 2014 (Zn, paywall); Li 2016 (Cd, paywall); Li 2014 (26,388 mg/kg, not located); Zhang 2011 (P. fortunei, not located); Torres 2008 (not verified). No value from these sources is cited as fact.

7.3. State of this axis

Moderate confidence and restricted scope: two integral primary sources (Cu and Pb in moso, specific test conditions); insufficient evidence to generalize to native bamboos, real soils or other species. Central gap: absence of field tests and of records for native species (Guadua spp.) with confirmed integral source.

8Standards, patents, market and industrialization in Brazil

8.1. Standards landscape

The thesis of Marçal (2018) compares international and foreign national standards applicable to bamboo culm: the standards share trends, but adapt species, parameters and practices to local realities; variability, taper and the absence of industrial standardization increase the complexity of design and execution; the author highlights the Ecuadorian standard as a broad reference in the studied time span; and a chain capable of delivering mature, selected, preserved and dried culms is a relevant condition for standardization. The NSR-10, Title G (2010) record registers the Colombian earthquake-resistant construction regulation that recognizes guadua as a regulated structural material (156 pages in the verified copy), integrating raw material, preservation, calculation and execution — with the record's caveat that the foreign standard does not authorize the design of Brazilian works nor replace ABNT and technical responsibility. The review of Adier et al. (2023) maps the evolution of codes (ISO 22157, ABNT NBR 16828, NSR-10) and points to the main gap of contemporary bamboo engineering: the lack of sustainable non-friable grouts in the connections to prevent shear at the nodes. The Brazilian testing and industrialization records cite the standards NBR 16828-1/2 (Oliveira 2025), NBR 7190/97, NBR 9531/86 and NBR 16828 (Martins 2021), and the record of Louredo et al. (2025) registers the standards NBR 16828:2020 and NBR 17043:2023.

Normative genealogy (India → ISO → Latin America). Marçal (2018) and the 2026 documentary update situate the body of standards for bamboo culm in a genealogy: the ISO 22156/22157 standards (ISO/TC 165 committee) and the Indian standard IS 15912 appear as formative references; NSR-10 (Colombia, 2010) is a regional landmark; and the NTE E.100 (Peru) and NEC-SE-GUADÚA (Ecuador) standards were published later, with their own adaptations — without implying automatic normative succession. The recorded editions are IS 15912:2018 (First Revision; 2012 was the first publication and is the edition analyzed by Marçal), ISO 22156:2021 and ISO 22157:2019 (protected; records only with metadata, scope and access condition). For Costa Rica, no applicable structural standard was located in the sources and delimited searches of this review; the 2022 article about a house built with Guadua and Dendrocalamus is constructive context, not a standard.

Andean scope comparison. NSR-10, NTE E.100 and NEC-SE-GUADÚA are national or regional technical regulations for bamboo. The earthquake-resistant dimension is described only where each standard actually addresses it; the story limits and other parameters must be verified separately in each document. The standards differ in target species, allowable stresses, characterization, connections and enclosures, therefore they are not interchangeable. IS 15912 deals with Indian species; the ISO 22156/22157 remain protected and are used here only as metadata reference, without integral reproduction.

Use in Brazil. The Andean and international reference provides a comparable map of stages (production, preservation, design, connections, seismic) useful to support a possible Brazilian standard, and reinforces Marçal's (2018) diagnosis that no specific equivalent ABNT standard was located, in the corpus of this review, for structural construction with bamboo. But Brazilian species, service classes, local seismic/wind, equilibrium moisture and supply chain require Brazilian validation (ISO 22157 is the species-independent laboratory protocol): no foreign standard equals ABNT and none replaces technical responsibility.

8.2. Production chain and market

The thesis of Lima (2019) mapped 222 productive and R&D initiatives with native bamboos (concentrated in Acre, Southeast and South), with a case study of 23 initiatives in Acre (interviews 2014–2016): institutional arrangements, policies and prior experience favored the initiatives; insufficient funding, discontinuity, limited knowledge and regulatory obstacles appeared as constraints; and the author observes lesser protagonism of local and socio-environmental actors in the analyzed networks. The record of Louredo, Pantoja and Teixeira (2025) — exploratory work of the XVIII EBRAMEM — compiles source estimates: 258 native species (35 genera, 68% endemic); Guadua reserves in Acre estimated at 21.8 billion stems (800.1 million m³, 62% of the state territory); natural supply valued at 4.4 billion dollars for boards and 778.5 million dollars for charcoal; and registers the legal framework (Law nº 12,484/2011 — PNMCB), the standards NBR 16828:2020 and NBR 17043:2023 and the work of the Rede Brasileira do Bambu. The Revista Bambu (RBB, n. 3, 2022) and the Bamboo and Rattan Update (INBAR, v. 6, n. 2, 2025) are records of institutional journals: useful for mapping actors and agendas (Seminário Nacional do Bambu, Rede Brasileira do Bambu; climate action, restoration, livelihoods, plastic substitution), but, as the records themselves register, their market or impact numbers should not be reused as scientific evidence without a primary source. The record of Teixeira et al. (2021) covers the base of the chain: micropropagation protocol of Bambusa vulgaris in a semi-hydroponic system, with 21.9% in vitro establishment of the nodal segments (9 collections between April 2017 and March 2018), greenhouse environment as the best donor (28.4%, versus 20.1% in the field and 14.3% in the shade house), fungal contamination as the main mortality factor, 80.0% survival and 50.0% adventitious rooting in MS medium without antibiotic, and absence of somaclonal variation by ISSR markers after 16 subcultures (~10 months).

8.3. Patents

The two patent letters in the drawer are primary technological sources, outside the scientific count: the external prestressing of bamboo culms (UFMG) and the capillary bamboo microreactor (Faculdades Católicas). Both records register that the grant protects novelty and inventive activity within the scope of the claims, but does not certify performance for general use — the documents lack specimen series, statistical comparison, botanical identification (species absent in both), durability and normative protocol.

8.4. State of this axis

Moderate confidence (documentary record); market estimates not audited by independent studies. The records support that Brazil has a legal framework (PNMCB, Law nº 12,484/2011), ABNT standards in force for bamboo structures (NBR 16828:2020; NBR 17043:2023) and an active institutional network (Rede Brasileira do Bambu, INBAR), but that the chain faces structural barriers: absence of commercial plantations, low processing yield (~30%), imported adhesives, lack of a specific standard for BaLC, PNMCB not regulated (Martins 2021; Louredo 2025; Lima 2019) and a gap of standards for engineered materials such as CLB (Alves 2025). The supply and market value estimates (Louredo 2025) come from the source, are exploratory in nature, and were not audited by independent studies in the drawer.

8.5. Public policies and technological sovereignty

The collection supports a policy agenda, not a ready-made policy. Law nº 12,484/2011, the Brazilian standards cited by the records and the production-chain records show that frameworks and initiatives already exist, but they do not demonstrate, by themselves, an integrated national chain of production, preservation, testing, design, execution, maintenance and final disposal of structural bamboo. A responsible policy should articulate research with Brazilian species, professional training, laboratories, culm traceability, pilot public procurement, technical assistance and post-occupancy monitoring.

Public support for cultivation and processing should be conditioned on management, genetic diversity, territorial rights, occupational safety, residue treatment and disposal. The adoption of foreign standards can guide comparable questions and methods, but does not replace Brazilian validation nor should it produce automatic technological dependence. The agenda of cooperatives, semi-industrial units and local chains remains a hypothesis of productive organization to be evaluated by its own economic, environmental and social studies.

8.6. Material, environmental and life-cycle sustainability

Bamboo is not automatically sustainable. The LCA of Araujo et al. (2025), in the studied artisanal system, points to relevant impact associated with borate effluents, leaching and contaminated residues; these results are from the analyzed model and unit, not a universal rate for every treatment. The EDA should consider, in any comparison, the origin and toxicity of preservatives, leaching, Class-1-potential shavings and residues, water consumption, energy and fuel, transport, VOCs when applicable formulations exist, durability, maintenance and end of life.

Heat treatments, pyroligneous acid, steam, alkalization and other routes appear as research paths, not as already-proven superior alternatives. The comparison will only be valid with species, moisture content, application method, concentration, time/temperature, performance, toxicity and LCA defined comparably. Without this set, one cannot claim lower carbon footprint, lower toxicity or environmental superiority.

8.7. Evidence, hypothesis and agenda

LayerWhat the collection allows saying
EvidenceThere is chain, treatment, testing, standards and LCA data, each restricted to its method and context.
HypothesisLower-impact routes, national management, heat/steam treatment and cooperative chains may reduce liabilities, but still require controlled comparison.
AgendaLeaching and toxicity tests; comparative LCA; energy/transport inventory; residue protocols; durability; Brazilian species; costs and governance of local chains.

None of these agendas equates to certification, structural safety, TRL or validated public policy.

Convergences of the documentary set

  • Thermal window. Independent records converge on a severity range in which heat treatment improves dimensional stability and delays biological attack without relevant mechanical loss, and on a limit beyond which the material degrades (Costa 2015; Wang et al. 2020; Shangguan et al. 2016; Oliveira et al. 2025).
  • Mechanical performance of transformed bamboo. Densification and laminates reach, at bench scale, flexural strengths far superior to those of the natural culm, with lamina orientation and bark retention as conditioning factors (Sá 2022; Tarverdi 2024; Rusch et al. 2019; Reghin Filho 2018).
  • Durability as a system property. On-site durability depends on design — moisture control, structural redundancy, inspection and maintenance — as much as on treatment (Bussinger 2024; CONTECC 2025, pathologies; Gutiérrez-González and Takeuchi-Tam 2014).
  • Absence of a Brazilian standard as a barrier. The lack of specific standards for engineered materials and the pending PNMCB regulation appear as obstacles in independent records (Marçal 2018; Martins 2021; Alves 2025; CONTECC 2025, natives).
  • Environmental impact of chemical processing. The "sustainability" of bamboo is not automatic: chemical treatment generates liabilities (borate effluents, leaching) that can dominate the life-cycle impact (Araujo et al. 2025; Gauss 2020).
  • Pyroligneous acid without demonstrated conformity. No record demonstrates the normative efficacy of pyroligneous acid: inconclusive in bamboo (Silva 2011), inconclusive in soil (Matsuoka & Beraldo 2014), rejected by the normative criterion applied in pine (Laroque 2022) — with the Embrapa Circular 65 recording that it does not demonstrate safety or efficacy.

9Controversies and gaps

Controversies

  • Efficacy of pyroligneous acid: demonstrated or inconclusive? The drawer contains a single Silva (2011) record (treatment against borers), which documents a 20-week test with BLC in dilutions of 10%, 20% and 30% without statistical difference between dilutions and the control. Added are Laroque (2022), which rejected the raw liquid by the adopted normative criterion (in pine), and Matsuoka & Beraldo (2014), inconclusive in soil. The documentary set does not allow claiming the normative preservative conformity of pyroligneous acid in bamboo.
  • Thermal window: where is the limit? Saturated steam shows relevant losses at 180 °C/30 min (Wang et al. 2020, high-temperature record); an oven shows 180 °C/4 h harmful in BLC (Costa 2015); the scrimber degrades above 170 °C (Shangguan et al. 2016); Oliveira et al. (2025), meanwhile, observes no relevant changes at 160–200 °C for 1–2 h — but with minimal sampling, without statistics. The partial divergence among sources as to the limit-severity must be declared in any normative use.

Resolution note (2026-08-01): the duplicities and registration divergences pointed out in previous versions were resolved — fabricated records removed (Silva 2011 "conservação"; Wang 2020 with nonexistent DOI -7) and duplicate reconciled (Araujo 2025). Records preserved in private backup. See correction log.

  • "Sustainable bamboo" versus processing liabilities. The LCA of Araujo et al. (2025), applied to an artisanal unit of Rio Branco-AC (cradle-to-gate, 1 kg of treated culm), estimates that human carcinogenic toxicity represented about 93% of the potential impact (borate effluents and chemical residues disposed of in soil) and that contaminated residues of shavings and disposed culms accounted for 91% of the total impact of the system, with about 10% of the hot chemical bath solution leached due to the lack of an impermeable floor. The record warns that the values describe the studied model and unit — but the controversy is real: the automatic "green" labeling of bamboo finds no documentary support in the drawer without an audit of the treatment process.
  • Bench evidence versus industrial scale. Densification, bioconcretes, composites and CLB have promising results in the laboratory (Sá 2022; Tarverdi 2024; Gangorra et al. 2024; Santos 2020; Alves 2025), but no record validates continuous production or long-duration on-site performance; the drawer's patents are propositional, and the "alignment with the Acervo technology" sections present in some records are authorial interpretation, not evidence.

Gaps

  • Long-duration field tests (weathering, fungi, insects) for heat and pyroligneous treatments in bamboo — the drawer only contains laboratory or short-duration tests.
  • Specific Brazilian standards for BaLC, densified bamboo and CLB; regulation of PNMCB (Martins 2021; Alves 2025).
  • CLB durability and standardization data (gap declared in Alves 2025).
  • Own mechanical characterization of native Amazonian species — the records use analogy with G. angustifolia and D. giganteus (CONTECC 2025).
  • LCA of alternative treatment routes (Boucherie, pyroligneous acid, heat treatment) — the very LCA by Araujo et al. (2025) declares it has not evaluated them.
  • Full-scale structural validation — seismic (Puma Alvarez 2014, 1:20 scale), prestressing (UFMG patent), reticular structures (Ruggiero 2021, simulation).
  • Chain economics — the supply and market value estimates (Louredo 2025) have no independent audit in the drawer.

10Synthesis and integration into the Acervo

The documentary set supports three strong findings. First: heat treatment is the best-documented preservation route in the drawer — multiple independent records (Costa 2015; Wang et al. 2020; Oliveira et al. 2025; Shangguan et al. 2016) converge on an operational window in which dimensional stability and durability improve without relevant mechanical loss, and on the existence of a severity limit beyond which the material degrades. Second: industrial transformation (densification, laminates, panels, CLB) has promising bench-scale evidence — with expressive numbers, such as MOR of ~312 MPa in Sá's (2022) densified element and 239.24 MPa in Tarverdi's (2024) panel —, but runs into normative and scale barriers in Brazil documented by Martins (2021) and Alves (2025). Third: on-site durability depends as much on treatment as on design, moisture control and maintenance (Bussinger 2024; Afonso 2025).

The set also imposes two honest findings. Pyroligneous acid remains laboratory evidence inconclusive as to normative conformity: the drawer registers the absence of statistical difference in the only controlled test in bamboo (Silva 2011), an inconclusive result in soil (Matsuoka & Beraldo 2014) and rejection by the only normative criterion applied (Laroque 2022, in pine). And the "sustainability" of bamboo is not automatic: the LCA of the Amazonian artisanal chain (Araujo et al. 2025) locates the dominant impact in the disposal of borate effluents, which strains any narrative of a material "green" by nature.

Within the Acervo, the axis directly feeds the critical synthesis of the Ecological and Technological Sovereignty Review Notebooks — Notebook 1 (preservation from a socio-ecological perspective), Notebook 2 (from the conditioned culm to the protected component) and Notebook 4 (from prototype to conformity) —, with the role separation that the Acervo requires: the records provide attributed evidence; the technology-alignment sections and the notebooks are authorial proposition. Curatorial interpretation: with the reconciliation of records concluded (2026-08-01, see section 8), the natural next steps of the drawer are (i) to convert this state of the art into an Evidence Map, a Gaps Map and a Research Agenda; and (ii) to prioritize the acquisition of sources that cover long-duration field tests and characterization of native Amazonian species, the two most costly gaps for the axis.

Methodological note: this document is a curatorial synthesis of already-recorded sources. Numbers, citations and interpretations are attributed to their respective source records, all with integral source verified and in the em-revisao-documental state. Patents, standards, journals, circulars and lectures do not enter the scientific count; simulation, laboratory test and experience report are evidence of different natures; and no documentary state equates to experimental validation by the Acervo. The duplicities and registration divergences pointed out in previous versions were resolved on 2026-08-01 (see section 8).

Relationship with the authorial agenda

The convergences, controversies and gaps of this State of the Art converse with the Ecological and Technological Sovereignty Review Notebooks and with other authorial instruments of Fabio Takwara.

These documents formulate hypotheses, investigation architectures, decision criteria and experimental agendas. They do not constitute independent evidence of performance of the proposed technologies and do not enter the count of studies that support the conclusions of this State of the Art.

The relationship between external evidence and authorial formulation is registered in the Traceability Matrix.

Nota editorial — instrumentos preservados

Las dos secciones siguientes — Mapa de evidencias (resumen) y Línea de tiempo (1990–2025) — son instrumentos del EDA preservados integralmente. Estos brindan trazabilidad histórica y un conteo temático independiente (total 51 en el Mapa de Evidencias). No son el corpus científico (54 fichas con fuente integral conferida); constituyen instrumentos que dialogan con la Parte 4 y con la transición a las evidencias técnicas (§2–§8). Quedan posicionados entre la Apertura editorial y el §2 técnico, mantenidos intactos.
